title: 日常协作先异步：把问题写清楚再约实时沟通
topic: 日常协作先异步：把问题写清楚再约实时沟通

source.title: How We Work — Asynchronously
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 本课完整呈现 37signals 员工手册 Chapter 3: How We Work。学习重点为 Asynchronously 小节：日常问题先用消息、待办或文档写清需要说明或了解的内容，让同事按自己的节奏阅读；异步沟通不合适时再实时协作。练习人物和产品问题为虚构情境。
paragraphs: Most of the work you do at 37signals shouldn’t require you to be in constant communication throughout the entire day with someone.

You should collaborate as though most things you ask of others will get an answer eventually, but not necessarily right this second. Your first choice of action should be to post a message, a todo, or a document about what you need to explain or need to know. Then others can read it on their schedule, when the natural lulls of the day allow it, rather than being interrupted right in their peak flow time.

Of course there will be times when you do need to tightly collaborate with someone in real time, but those cases should be infrequent. We have pings, video calls, screen-sharing, or even in-person collaboration for when async isn’t efficient.
translations: 在 37signals，你的大部分工作不应要求你整天与某个人保持持续沟通。
与他人协作时，可以假设多数问题最终会得到答复，但不一定马上得到。首先可以发一条消息、一项待办或一份文档，写清你需要说明或了解的内容。这样其他人能按自己的安排、在工作节奏自然放缓时阅读，而不是在专注工作时被打断。
当然，有时确实需要与人紧密实时协作，但这种情况应该不常见。如果异步沟通效率不高，可以用即时消息、视频通话、屏幕共享，甚至当面协作。

fullChapterParagraphs: 37signals is a fully distributed company. Our team works from all over the world, across 5 continents. We don’t care where employees choose to live and work, just that they’re here to do great work on exceptional products, alongside a world-class team. We’ve been remote since we started, and our founders literally wrote the book on the subject.
You can work from anywhere, but please be sure to inform your People Ops team when you move – especially across state or country borders. It may affect your or the company’s tax situation.

We work in 6-week cycles at 37signals. This fixed cadence serves to give us an internal sense of urgency, to keep projects from ballooning, and to provide us with a regular interval to make decisions about what we’re working on.

Our cycle structure is particularly important for the product teams, since they approach feature and product development with scope and budget in mind up front. For more on this, all employees are encouraged to read Shape Up.
All teams operate on the same 6-week cadence.

In between each cycle, we spend two weeks cooling down. That’s when product teams deal with bugs, when everyone writes up what they’ve worked on, and when teams decide what to tackle next. Sometimes big batch projects extend into cool down, but we try to avoid that.
Since we work asynchronously and remotely, it’s important to radiate information about what we’re working on. We have 4 chief mechanisms for doing that.

What did you work on today? You’ll be asked this question every afternoon, and you’re required to answer at least twice a week. You should describe what you’re working on and give some context about why you’re working on it or why it’s important.
What will you be working on this week? You’ll be asked this question every Monday morning, and you’re required to answer every week.

Daily and weekly check-ins are subdivided by department so you’re only subscribed to your team’s answers. You’re of course free to subscribe to other team check-ins, but you’re not obligated to do so if you find it too noisy.

Every team submits a Kickoff for the upcoming cycle, and they’re due the second Friday of the cooldown period. Teams use their kickoff to summarize the work they have scheduled for the upcoming cycle.

Heartbeats are required of every team, and they’re due on the first Friday of the cooldown period. Teams use their heartbeat to summarize and celebrate the work they completed during the previous cycle, and the work described in the cycle heartbeat should line up (more or less) with the work you scheduled in the cycle kickoff.

These 4 mechanisms work together to free individuals and teams to run their days and cycles with confidence and independence. We have six opportunities per year to make big decisions about what to work on, and the rest of the time should chiefly be spent carrying out those short-term plans. By having clear expectations for communication, it’s easier for everyone to build trust in where we’re going and why.

Heartbeats and Kickoffs are assigned to team leads well in advance of every cycle. Heartbeats, kickoffs, and automatic check-in answers can all be found in the What Works project for the current year.
Most of the work you do at 37signals shouldn’t require you to be in constant communication throughout the entire day with someone.

You should collaborate as though most things you ask of others will get an answer eventually, but not necessarily right this second. Your first choice of action should be to post a message, a todo, or a document about what you need to explain or need to know. Then others can read it on their schedule, when the natural lulls of the day allow it, rather than being interrupted right in their peak flow time.

Of course there will be times when you do need to tightly collaborate with someone in real time, but those cases should be infrequent. We have pings, video calls, screen-sharing, or even in-person collaboration for when async isn’t efficient.
We rely on everyone at 37signals to do a lot of self-management. People who do this well are managers of one, and we expect everyone to embody this principle.

That means setting your own direction when one isn’t given; and determining what needs to be done, and doing it, without waiting for someone to tell you to. A manager of one will spend their time well when left to their own devices. There’s always more work to be done, always more initiatives to kick off, and always more improvement to be had.

We limit ourselves to a 40-hour (32-hour in the summer) work week. Keeping our hours at work limited forces us to prioritize the work that really matters. A healthy amount of sleep and a rich and rewarding life outside of work should not be squandered for a few more hours at work.

There are occasions when teams or individuals need to work off-hours for on-call, maintenance, or emergencies. This time should not be in addition to your normal working hours. Use your discretion to take time off to make up for the additional hours you put in during the week.

notes.explain: 这里强调大多数工作不需要一整天都与他人实时保持联系。
notes.example: Routine questions do not require constant communication.

notes.meaning: 按他们自己的时间安排
notes.explain: 异步消息允许收件人在合适的工作间隙阅读，不表示可以永远不回复。
notes.example: Please post the details so the team can read them on their schedule.

notes.meaning: 工作节奏自然放缓的空当
notes.explain: 同事可在手头工作暂歇时查看，而不是在专注时被打断。
notes.example: I’ll review your message during a natural lull in my day.

notes.explain: 可用于确实需要紧密协作、异步方式不够高效的情况。
notes.example: If async is not efficient, we can talk in real time.

scenario.title: A teammate asks for an immediate call about a routine question
english: A teammate sends you a ping and asks you to stop your work for a call about a routine product question.
The question is not urgent, and they can explain it in a message or a to-do.
You suggest writing down the question and context, letting each person read it on their schedule, and talking in real time only if async is not efficient.
chinese: 一位同事发来即时消息，要求你停下手头工作，马上开会讨论一个常规产品问题。
问题并不紧急，对方可以在消息或待办里写清问题和背景。
你建议先写下问题和背景，让双方按自己的时间阅读；只有异步沟通不够高效时再实时讨论。

firstAttempt.prompt: 同事为一个不紧急的常规问题要求马上开会。请用英文建议他先把问题和背景写在消息、待办或文档里；说明你会在工作间隙阅读，并表示异步沟通不合适时可以实时讨论。
firstAttempt.sample: Since it isn’t urgent, could you post a message, a to-do, or a document explaining what you need to know? I’ll read it when I have a natural lull in my day. If async isn’t efficient, we can talk in real time.
firstAttempt.rationale: 回答包含先写清问题、给同事按自己的节奏阅读，以及异步不合适时再实时沟通三步。

words.meaning: 异步地；不要求同时在线地
words.example: The remote team works asynchronously across time zones.
words.translation: 远程团队跨时区异步协作。
words.note: 沟通双方不必同时在线，也不期待立即回复。

words.meaning: 按某人自己的时间安排
words.example: The team can read the update on their schedule.
words.translation: 团队成员可以按自己的时间安排阅读更新。
words.note: 强调异步安排，不代表忽略消息。

words.meaning: 暂时平静；工作节奏放缓的空当
words.collocation: a natural lull in the day
words.example: I’ll review the document during a natural lull in my day.
words.translation: 我会在当天工作节奏自然放缓时查看文档。
words.note: 这里指手头工作暂歇的时段，不一定是正式休息时间。

words.example: Let’s collaborate in real time if async is not efficient.
words.translation: 如果异步沟通效率不高，我们就实时协作。
words.note: 来源建议只在确有需要时使用同步方式。

structure.original: Your first choice of action should be to post a message, a todo, or a document about what you need to explain or need to know.
analysis: Your first choice of action 是主语，指“首先采取的做法”。
should be to post... 是系动词加不定式表语，说明首选做法是发布消息、待办或文档。
about what you need to explain or need to know 说明发布内容应写清要解释或了解的事。
structure.transfer: Could you post a message with the launch question and the context? I’ll review it when I have a natural lull. If async isn’t efficient, we can talk in real time.

rewrite.bad: Stop what you are doing and join my call right now. I need an answer to a routine question.
rewrite.good: Could you post a message, a to-do, or a document explaining what you need to know? I’ll read it when I have a natural lull in my day. If async isn’t efficient, we can talk in real time.
rewrite.translation: 你能把需要了解的问题写在消息、待办或文档里吗？我会在当天工作节奏自然放缓时查看。如果异步沟通效率不高，我们可以实时聊。
rewrite.pattern: Could you post [the question and context]? I’ll read it [when I have a natural lull]. If async isn’t efficient, we can [talk in real time].

cloze.prompt: Your first choice should be to ___ a message, a todo, or a document.
cloze.why: 来源建议先发布消息、待办或文档，把需要说明或了解的内容写下来。

cloze.prompt: Others can read it on their ___.
cloze.why: on their schedule 表示收件人可按自己的时间安排阅读。

cloze.prompt: We can collaborate in real time when async isn’t ___.
cloze.why: 来源把实时协作留给异步方式不够高效的情况。

dictation.text: Your first choice of action should be to post a message, a todo, or a document about what you need to explain or need to know.
dictation.label: 听写 1 · 先写清问题
dictation.why: 听辨 first choice of action 和三个异步沟通载体。

dictation.text: Then others can read it on their schedule, when the natural lulls of the day allow it.
dictation.label: 听写 2 · 按自己的节奏阅读
dictation.why: 抓住 on their schedule 和 natural lulls，理解不要求立即同步。

apply.prompt: 同事为常规问题要求马上通话。请建议对方先发消息，并说明你会在工作节奏稍缓时查看。
apply.sample: Could you post a message with the question and context? I’ll read it when I have a natural lull in my day.

translationPractice.prompt: 你能把需要说明或了解的问题写在消息里吗？
translationPractice.answer: Could you post a message about what you need to explain or know?
translationPractice.why: post a message about 后接要写清的主题；这里保留来源中的 explain or know。

translationPractice.prompt: 我会在当天工作节奏自然放缓时查看。
translationPractice.answer: I’ll read it when I have a natural lull in my day.
translationPractice.why: a natural lull 指工作节奏暂时放缓的空当，不承诺立刻回复。

translationPractice.prompt: 如果异步沟通效率不高，我们可以实时聊。
translationPractice.answer: We can talk in real time if async isn’t efficient.
translationPractice.why: in real time 表示同步沟通；if 从句明确这是异步不够高效时的选择。

choice.prompt: 同事为一个不紧急的常规问题要求马上开会。你想先异步沟通，并保留必要时实时讨论的选项。请选择合适的回复。
options: Please keep pinging me until I stop my work and answer immediately.
Could you post a message with the question and context? I’ll read it when I have a natural lull. If async isn’t efficient, we can talk in real time.
We should never talk in real time, even when async is not efficient.
choice.why: 正确项先提供异步渠道、允许按工作节奏阅读，并保留异步不高效时实时协作的选择。

output.prompt: 另一个团队需要你对一项发布问题提供背景，但并不需要马上做决定。请用英文请对方把问题和背景写进消息或待办；说明你会在工作间隙阅读，并表示如果异步沟通不够高效，可以实时讨论。
output.sample: Could you post a message or a to-do with the launch question and its context? I’ll review it when I have a natural lull in my day. If async isn’t efficient, we can talk in real time.
check: 是否请对方先写下问题和背景？
是否说明你会按自己的工作节奏查看？
是否仅在异步不够高效时提出实时讨论？
